slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Single fixed-offset record at EEPROM offset 0; no alternate slot, backup copy, or generation counter found in traced code (FUN_0800dce0/FUN_0800dddc always operate at absolute offset 0).

checksums.name: record_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: FUN_0800d9cc(ptr, len): backward byte-wise accumulator. uVar2=len-1; iVar4=0; pb=ptr+len-2; repeat len-1 times: uVar2 += buf[pb] + iVar4; iVar4 = uVar2>>8; uVar2 = (uVar2 & 0xff) ^ buf[pb+1]; pb-=1. Return low byte of uVar2 (upper byte always 0). Called as FUN_0800d9cc(record+2, 0x16) i.e. covers record bytes [0x02,0x18).

io_driver_functions.notes: AGB-style multi-backend save dispatcher: bounds-checks backend type 0-3 and fetches a 4-byte descriptor; both call sites pass type=3 (EEPROM).
Generic DMA3 (0x040000D4 region) transfer-and-busy-wait primitive used by both EEPROM read and write bit-stream drivers.
IME-style critical-section enter (disable) helper wrapping the EEPROM write bit-banging sequence.
IME-style critical-section exit (restore) helper, counterpart to 0x0803031c.
EEPROM read primitive: serializes a 14-bit read address, issues DMA3 request to 0x0D000000, deserializes 64 bits back into 4x u16 words. Reads one 8-byte page.

EEPROM write primitive: serializes address + 64-bit payload into a write-command bit-stream, issues via DMA3 to 0x0D000000, polls busy flag. Writes one 8-byte page. No static caller resolved in callgraph.json (indirect/jump-table call), identified by unique write-sequence behavior.
Write-verify: reads back a page via 0x08030468 and compares against expected data; returns 0 on match, 0x8000 on mismatch.
SaveWriteBlock(offset,size): selects EEPROM backend via 0x080302e4, writes then verifies every 8-byte page in range. Called with (0, 0x18).
SaveReadBlock(offset,size): selects EEPROM backend via 0x080302e4, reads every 8-byte page in range into destination buffer. Called with (0, 0x18).

Top-level WriteSaveRecord: builds 24-byte struct in RAM from live gameplay globals, computes checksum, flushes via 0x08003730. No static caller resolved (reached via indirect/jump-table dispatch, e.g. a save menu handler).

Top-level ReadSaveRecord: reads 24-byte struct via 0x08003798, verifies checksum then an offset-0x02 gate value against a fixed RAM constant, and only then deserializes into live gameplay globals. No static caller resolved.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Unresolved (indirect call, likely a save-menu/checkpoint event handler not captured by static callgraph.json edges)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Grep for direct callers of the EEPROM block-write function 0x08003730 in decompiled.c located exactly one call site at line ~2544, inside FUN_0800dce0, which also calls the checksum routine 0x0800d9cc immediately prior. Confirmed by matching the function's write offsets against the save profile's single active range 0x0000-0x0017.

fields.name: record_checksum
fields.update_mechanism: Computed by FUN_0800d9cc over bytes [0x02,0x18) immediately before the 24-byte record is flushed to EEPROM.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c lines ~2540-2544 (write), ~2580-2582 (read-compare); formula did not reproduce on the one real sample (see save-format.json checksums[0].verified_on_samples).

fields.name: gate_value
fields.update_mechanism: Copied from an unresolved RAM source (_DAT_0800dd6c) on save; on load, compared for exact equality against a fixed RAM constant (uRam0800de8c) and gates whether the rest of the record is deserialized.

fields.name: index_selector
fields.update_mechanism: Copied from unresolved RAM source (_DAT_0800dd70) on save; on load, passed to FUN_080032b0(idx) which stores idx and computes a pointer base+idx*8 (no bounds check observed).
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c line 2506 (write), line 2584 (read) and FUN_080032b0 body at line 1245.

fields.name: byte_field_6
fields.update_mechanism: Direct byte copy both directions, no transform.

fields.name: byte_field_7_config_param
fields.update_mechanism: Direct byte copy on save; on load, passed as an argument into func_0x08002978 rather than stored directly (callee not traced in this corpus).
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c line 2508 (write), line 2586 (read, passed to func_0x08002978).

fields.name: raw_array_8_12
fields.update_mechanism: Raw memcpy both directions (unresolved RAM source _DAT_0800dd88 on save, destination iRam0800dea8 on load); no checksum or transform applied to these bytes individually.

fields.name: byte_field_13
fields.update_mechanism: Direct byte copy both directions, no transform.

fields.name: byte_field_14
fields.update_mechanism: Direct byte copy both directions, no transform.

fields.name: byte_field_15
fields.update_mechanism: Direct byte copy both directions, no transform.

fields.name: packed_status_byte
fields.update_mechanism: On save: 4 unresolved u16 source values (_DAT_0800dd8c array) are each mapped to a 2-bit code (value 2 -> code 1, value 0x100 -> code 3, value 0x200 -> code 2, else -> code 0) and packed MSB-first into one byte. On load: each 2-bit sub-field indexes a 4-entry u16 lookup table, writing the result into RAM array iRam0800dea0.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c lines ~2519-2541 (pack, write side), lines ~2592-2601 (unpack, read side).

fields.name: reserved_padding_11_16
fields.update_mechanism: Zeroed implicitly by the leading memset in FUN_0800dce0; never individually written or read by any traced function.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c line 2504 (memset(puVar2,0,0x18)); absence of any further write/read at offsets 0x11-0x16 confirmed by full-function read-through.

fields.name: anomalous_tail_byte
fields.update_mechanism: UNKNOWN. Covered by the checksum's declared range (bytes [0x02,0x18)) but never explicitly written by FUN_0800dce0 (which writes only offsets 0x00-0x10 and otherwise relies on the leading memset-to-zero) nor explicitly read by FUN_0800dddc. Its nonzero value in the real sample is unexplained by any function in this 181-function trace and may be the cause of the checksum-verification mismatch in checksums[0].
fields.evidence: Hex comparison of saves/cap-01-future-1.sav offset 0x17 against full read-through of FUN_0800dce0 (ghidra/decompiled.c lines 2488-2557), which has no store to offset 0x17.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip bits in stored checksum, leave payload unchanged
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Load aborts at the checksum-compare branch in FUN_0800dddc; no gameplay RAM written.
If this is genuinely a fixed version/magic gate, load aborts after checksum passes but before FUN_080032b0 runs; distinguishes gate field from ordinary gameplay data.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: set to 0x0000 and to 0x7fff, repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: FUN_080032b0 computes base+idx*8 with no observed bounds check; large index may read/corrupt unrelated RAM, confirming the field is an unchecked table selector.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: set each byte to 0xff and 0x00 individually, repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Values should appear unmodified in RAM array iRam0800dea8 immediately after load, since this range has no pack/transform logic.
Each 2-bit sub-field should independently select one of 4 discrete states via the unpack lookup table; expect 4 discrete, not continuous, behavior changes.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: set offsets 0x11-0x16 to non-zero garbage, repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If truly unused, post-load gameplay state should be bit-identical to a load with these bytes left at 0x00.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: set to 0x00 vs leave at captured 0xd2, in both cases recomputing checksum per the decompiled formula
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Key counterfactual for the checksum-mismatch anomaly: determines whether the decompiled formula is correct and 0xd2 was written post-checksum by an untraced path, or whether the formula itself is wrong.

open_questions: Why does the real sample's stored checksum (0x0002) not match recomputation (0x00a5) under the fully-decompiled FUN_0800d9cc formula over bytes [0x02,0x18)?
What writes offset 0x17 (observed 0xd2), since no function in this 181-function trace touches it?
What are the real EWRAM/IWRAM addresses behind the unresolved _DAT_0800dd6c..dd8c and de90..dea8 literal-pool pointers?
What does the offset-0x04 table index (FUN_080032b0, base+idx*8) actually select, and is it range-checked anywhere outside the traced functions?
What gameplay-visible state corresponds to each of the 4 packed 2-bit codes at offset 0x10?
Is FUN_0800dce0/FUN_0800dddc reached via a save/load menu dispatch table, and if so, are there other entries representing a second, untraced save path?
